import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.Hadamard

/-!
# The circulant Hadamard conjecture

A circulant matrix is generated by cyclically shifting one row. The circulant Hadamard conjecture,
also attributed to Ryser, says that no circulant Hadamard matrix has order greater than $4$.

*Reference:*
* S. Steinerberger,
  [A note on approximate Hadamard matrices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13202)
-/

namespace CirculantHadamard

/-- A generator for a circulant Hadamard matrix of order four. -/
def orderFourGenerator : Fin 4 → ℝ :=
  ![1, 1, 1, -1]

/-- The order-four generator gives a circulant Hadamard matrix. -/
@[category test, AMS 15]
theorem orderFourGenerator_isHadamard :
    Hadamard.IsHadamard' (Matrix.circulant orderFourGenerator) := by
  constructor
  · intro i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      norm_num [Matrix.circulant, orderFourGenerator, Fin.sub_def, Fin.neg_def]
  · ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      norm_num [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.circulant, orderFourGenerator, Fin.sum_univ_succ,
        Fin.sub_def, Fin.neg_def, Matrix.ofNat_apply]

/-- Every circulant Hadamard matrix has order at most four. -/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem circulant_hadamard_conjecture {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hv : Hadamard.IsHadamard' (Matrix.circulant v)) : n ≤ 4 := by
  sorry

end CirculantHadamard

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over generators for all natural orders and uses the column-Gram condition MᵀM = nI. The source describes matrices with orthogonal rows and asserts nonexistence for n > 4.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Matrix.circulant uses exactly the source's indexing Mᵢⱼ = v(i−j mod n). For ±1 entries, each row has squared length n, so row orthogonality is equivalent to MMᵀ = nI. A circulant's transpose is circulant, and real circulants commute, giving MMᵀ = MᵀM. Bounding every admissible order by four is therefore equivalent to the source's nonexistence assertion. Including n = 0 adds only the true conclusion 0 ≤ 4. The full equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without sorryAx or reliance on the conjecture.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2402.13202 — Steinerberger, A Note on Approximate Hadamard Matrices; extracted approxhada.tex, including the definitions, ordinary Ryser conjecture, and subsequent remarks and quantitative variants.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadamard_matrix — definition, Gram-matrix characterization, and circulant Hadamard section.
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The order-four generator is valid, and orderFourGenerator_isHadamard has no sorry dependency. Inspected Hadamard.IsHadamard', Matrix.circulant, Fin subtraction, and matrix natural-number casts. Scratch proofs check orders zero and one and confirm that adding the empty order does not change the conjecture. Exhaustive Lean evaluation of integer ±1 generators for orders 0–8 gives counts [1, 2, 0, 0, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0], consistent with the intended definitions. The file faithfully states the ordinary conjecture explicitly posed in the paper's abstract and §1.1, rather than its separately presented quantitative variants. Both the cited paper and the consulted encyclopedia record the conjecture as open. The reviewed file matches the committed version.
